title: Avo-7-part-1
description: Avionics instrument systems, synchro systems, pressure sensing, aircraft instrument indications, displays, mounting, illumination, and airworthiness requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to move the indicator pointer of a synchro system?
questions.explanation: The receiver rotor converts the received electrical signals into mechanical movement to move the indicator pointer.

questions.question: Is a type of AC synchro system:
questions.explanation: Torque synchro systems are a type of AC synchro system used to transmit angular position.

questions.question: Desynn synchro system is a:
questions.explanation: The Desynn synchro system is a DC type of remote indication system.

questions.question: The most important instrument used by the pilot to perceive the health of an engine:
questions.explanation: Oil pressure indication provides an important indication of engine lubrication and operating condition.

questions.question: Which of the elastic pressure sensing elements is used for air data system:
questions.explanation: A capsule is an elastic pressure-sensing element commonly used in air data instruments.

questions.question: Two wires used in a simple single-phase synchro system are for:
questions.explanation: The two wires in a simple single-phase synchro system supply the exciter winding.

questions.question: Direct indication system is used on:
questions.explanation: Direct indication systems are commonly used on light aircraft because the sensing unit can be connected directly to the instrument.

questions.question: Bourdon tube's movable end straightens when:
questions.explanation: As pressure increases inside a Bourdon tube, its curved shape tends to straighten, producing movement for indication.

questions.question: Bourdon tube's open end that received the source of pressure is:
questions.explanation: The pressure is introduced through the fixed end of the Bourdon tube, while the other end is free to move.

questions.question: Indication system that involves data being transmitted electrically to the indication element:
questions.explanation: Remote sensing and indication transmits information electrically from the sensing location to the indicator.

questions.question: Which one is true about the first aircraft:
questions.explanation: The earliest aircraft designs did not have the conventional enclosed cockpit found in modern aircraft.

questions.question: 1st procedure in maintenance:
questions.explanation: Depressurization is performed first where applicable to remove stored pressure and make maintenance safer.

questions.question: Horizontal situation indicator:
questions.explanation: The horizontal situation indicator provides directional and navigation information to the pilot.

questions.question: Direct pressure reading for light single engine aircraft measuring:
questions.explanation: The provided answer is Coupling--, referring to the stated coupling element associated with the indication system.

questions.question: Serves as a controlling device against which deflecting forces are balanced:
questions.explanation: A hairspring provides controlling force that balances the deflecting force and helps return the indicating mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is found on the Wright Flyer:
questions.explanation: The Wright Flyer used basic instruments including an engine tachometer, anemometer, and stopwatch.

questions.question: Why were development and subsequent operation established with requirements and standards:
options: A. To eliminate all aircraft instruments
C. Environmental conditions require conformity of designs
questions.explanation: Aircraft instruments must operate reliably under demanding environmental conditions, requiring designs to conform to established requirements and standards.

questions.question: Which type of instruments are used to control the aircraft's flight attitude:
questions.explanation: Flight instruments provide the information needed to control and monitor aircraft attitude and flight.

questions.question: The basis of synchro systems operation is:
options: A. Electricity can be used to create magnetic fields
B. Hydraulic pressure creates electrical current
questions.explanation: Synchro operation is based on the relationship between electrical currents and magnetic fields.

questions.question: Which of the following is a DC synchro system:
questions.explanation: The Basic synchro system is identified as a DC synchro system in the provided material.

questions.question: Which type of displays follow the square-law or logarithmic law:
questions.explanation: Non-linear displays do not have a constant relationship between input and displayed value and may follow square-law or logarithmic characteristics.

questions.question: The Bourdon tube pointer is attached to:
questions.explanation: The pointer mechanism is connected to the movable portion of the Bourdon tube so its movement can be indicated.

questions.question: Where should power plant instrument be located:
options: B. Center of forward instrument panel visible to both pilots
questions.explanation: Powerplant instruments should be positioned where both pilots can readily see important engine indications.

questions.question: Why is remote indication system preferred for fuel pressure indication system:
options: A. It makes the fuel pressure higher
B. It removes the need for a sensor
C. Not safe to run a fuel line into cockpit--
questions.explanation: Remote indication avoids routing a pressurized fuel line into the cockpit, reducing the risk of fuel leakage and fire.

questions.question: How many flight instruments:
questions.explanation: The basic flight instrument grouping consists of six instruments.

questions.question: Commonly pneumatic pressure sensing system:
questions.explanation: Pneumatic pressure sensing systems commonly use remotely reading arrangements to transmit pressure information to the indicator.

questions.question: Part of T-shape indicator:
questions.explanation: The T-shaped basic flight instrument arrangement includes the airspeed indicator and altimeter among its main elements.

questions.question: Risk of direct reading of fuel:
options: A. Leakage in cockpit or cabin
questions.explanation: Direct fuel pressure or fuel-system indications can require fuel lines in the occupied area, creating a leakage hazard.

questions.question: Synchro described:
questions.explanation: A synchro is an electromechanical system used to measure, transmit, and transform angular position information.

questions.question: Powered by turbine engine:
questions.explanation: Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) is a parameter used as an indication of power or thrust in turbine engines.

questions.question: Coefficient of expansion of brass when exposed to ΔT:
questions.explanation: Brass has a relatively high coefficient of linear thermal expansion, so its dimensions change noticeably with temperature.

questions.question: Describe instrument mechanism:
options: A. A single instrument always has one element
B. Dual instrument can refer to 2 or 3 elements in one unit
C. Instrument mechanisms contain only electrical elements
questions.explanation: A dual instrument can combine two or sometimes three instrument elements into one physical unit.

questions.question: Can possibly affect if cabin pressure enter the case:
options: A. Instruments using only hydraulic pressure
C. Instrument using external atmospheric pressure as datum
questions.explanation: An instrument that uses external atmospheric pressure as a reference can be affected if cabin pressure enters its case.

questions.question: Belongs to hair spring:
questions.explanation: The hairspring belongs to the indicating mechanism and provides controlling force.

questions.question: Correct about torque synchro:
options: B. Receiver rotor free to rotate
questions.explanation: In a torque synchro system, the receiver rotor is free to rotate and follows the angular position transmitted by the transmitter.

questions.question: Made of two diaphragms:
questions.explanation: A capsule is formed by joining two diaphragms together around their edges.

questions.question: Pressure minus absolute zero pressure:
questions.explanation: Absolute pressure is referenced to absolute zero pressure, or a perfect vacuum.

questions.question: Instrument mechanism system that combines all four elements in one case:
questions.explanation: A direct sensing instrument system combines the detecting, measuring, coupling, and indicating elements in one case.

questions.question: Correct about Bourdon tube:
options: A. For low pressures, tube is always rigid
C. For high pressures, tube designed stiff
questions.explanation: Bourdon tubes used for high-pressure measurement are designed with sufficient stiffness to withstand the pressure.

questions.question: At what cabin altitude will a cabin altitude warning switch close:
questions.explanation: The provided answer is 10,000 ft MSL, the specified altitude at which the cabin altitude warning switch closes.

questions.question: Sensor most suited for differential pressure measurement:
questions.explanation: The provided answer is Be lows, referring to the bellows-type pressure-sensing element used for differential pressure measurement.

questions.question: Correct statement:
options: A. Higher fuel-air mixture pressure → less power
B. Higher fuel-air mixture pressure → more power
C. Fuel-air mixture pressure has no effect on power
questions.explanation: In a reciprocating engine, increased mixture pressure entering the cylinders can increase the amount of charge and therefore engine power.

questions.question: Pressure sensor for hydraulic pressure indication system:
questions.explanation: Bourdon tubes are commonly used to sense and indicate hydraulic pressure.

questions.question: Instrument with flange mounting type:
questions.explanation: Flange mounting is a method in which the instrument is secured to the panel using its flange.

questions.question: Instruments included in basic six grouping:
options: A. Fuel pressure indicator, oil temperature
B. Vertical speed indicator, gyro horizon
questions.explanation: The vertical speed indicator and gyro horizon are among the six basic flight instruments.

questions.question: How does stator of TX synchro receive voltage:
questions.explanation: The transmitter stator receives induced voltage through magnetic coupling between the rotor magnetic field and stator windings.

questions.question: Methods of instrument mounting on panel:
questions.explanation: The two common methods of mounting instruments on a panel are flange mounting and clamp mounting.

questions.question: Instruments contributing info to guide aircraft along course:
questions.explanation: The horizontal situation display provides navigation information used to guide the aircraft along its intended course.

questions.question: Manifold pressure is:
questions.explanation: Manifold pressure is measured as absolute pressure, referenced to a perfect vacuum.

questions.question: Standard for requirements of instruments:
questions.explanation: Instrument requirements and standards include environmental conformity and appropriate design to ensure reliable operation.

questions.question: High-range, long-scale displays example:
questions.explanation: An altimeter is an example of a high-range, long-scale display because it covers a large range of altitude values.

questions.question: Bourdon tube connected to hose acts as:
questions.explanation: The Bourdon tube detects pressure and its resulting movement provides the measuring function.

questions.question: Take-off & precaution arc:
questions.explanation: The yellow arc is the caution or precaution range on an aircraft instrument.

questions.question: Parameter instrument grouping specific powerplant:
questions.explanation: Powerplant instrument grouping depends on the type of powerplant and the size/type of aircraft.

questions.question: Paralax error occurrence depends on:
questions.explanation: Parallax error occurs when the instrument is viewed from an angle rather than directly in line with the indication.

questions.question: In synchro, all transmitters located at:
questions.explanation: The synchro transmitter is located at the source of the measurement so it can sense and transmit the position.

questions.question: Oxygen pressure system transducer:
questions.explanation: A solid state device can be used as a transducer to convert oxygen pressure into an electrical signal.

questions.question: In reciprocating engine pressure interpreted as power:
questions.explanation: Torque pressure is the provided parameter associated with interpreting engine power in the reciprocating engine context.

questions.question: Engine oil pressure detected by:
questions.explanation: A Bourdon tube is commonly used to sense engine oil pressure and convert pressure into mechanical movement.

questions.question: Gyrohorizon:
questions.explanation: The gyrohorizon provides an indication of aircraft pitch and roll attitude.

questions.question: Remote indicating system using AC:
questions.explanation: Autosyn and Magnesyn are AC remote indicating systems used to transmit indications electrically.

questions.question: Flight heading & altitude instruments located on panels:
questions.explanation: The provided answer identifies panels P1 and P3 as the locations for flight heading and altitude instruments.

questions.question: Glare shield panel:
questions.explanation: The glare shield panel is identified as P5 in the provided aircraft panel arrangement.

questions.question: Sloping main instrument panel forward angle:
questions.explanation: The main instrument panel slopes forward by 15 degrees as specified in the provided material.

questions.question: Elastic pressure measuring unit for low pressure:
questions.explanation: A capsule is suitable for measuring relatively low pressures because its flexible diaphragms can respond to small pressure changes.

questions.question: Sector gear activated by:
questions.explanation: The sector gear receives movement from the measuring and coupling elements to operate the indication mechanism.

questions.question: Arrow on synchro schematic:
options: C. Direction of rotor rotation only
questions.explanation: The arrow shown on the synchro schematic indicates the direction of current flow.

questions.question: Movement of indicating element proportional to:
questions.explanation: The movement of the indicating element depends on the mechanical leverage, including the lever length.

questions.question: Gyro-horizon display:
options: A. Direct display of pitch, bank, roll
B. Display of fuel pressure only
C. Display of engine RPM only
questions.explanation: The gyro-horizon directly displays aircraft attitude, particularly pitch and bank/roll.

questions.question: Engine instruments located at center of:
questions.explanation: Engine instruments are positioned at the center of the main instrument panel for easy visibility.

questions.question: Receiver of synchro is:
questions.explanation: The synchro receiver operates like a motor, converting electrical signals into mechanical angular movement.

questions.question: Engine no.1 RPM indicator located at left of:
questions.explanation: The engine No. 1 RPM indicator is positioned to the left of the engine No. 2 RPM indicator.

questions.question: Illumination using two cover glasses:
questions.explanation: The wedge type illumination arrangement uses two cover glasses to distribute light.

questions.question: Requirement of instrument illumination system:
options: A. Maximum brightness at all times
questions.explanation: Instrument illumination must provide sufficient visibility without producing glare that could interfere with the pilot's vision.

questions.question: First successful airplanes flown by pioneers:
questions.explanation: Early successful aircraft used simple control arrangements such as sticks and strings.

questions.question: Airworthiness requirements and standards established by:
questions.explanation: Airworthiness requirements and standards are established by the appropriate authority of the country of design origin.

questions.question: Turbo prop engine power indicator:
questions.explanation: Torque is a primary indication of power produced by a turboprop engine.

questions.question: Measurement of one unknown pressure vs another:
questions.explanation: Differential pressure is the difference between two pressures and is used when one pressure is compared with another.

questions.question: Bourdon tube connected to hose acts as:
questions.explanation: When the Bourdon tube is directly connected to the pressure source through a hose, it forms a direct sensing arrangement.

questions.question: Elastic pressure sensing element for oxygen pressure indication:
questions.explanation: A Bourdon tube is an elastic pressure-sensing element suitable for oxygen pressure indication.

questions.question: Electrical zero of torque synchro system:
questions.explanation: The electrical zero position of the torque synchro system is 0 degrees.

questions.question: Electrical zero of control synchro system:
questions.explanation: The electrical zero position of a control synchro system is 90 degrees.

questions.question: T° compensation welding two metals strip:
questions.explanation: A bimetal strip consists of two different metals joined together and uses their different thermal expansion rates for temperature compensation.

questions.question: Screws used to mount instruments:
questions.explanation: Non-ferrous screws are used for instrument mounting to reduce magnetic effects and corrosion concerns.

questions.question: Engine type with thrust indicator:
questions.explanation: Turbojet engines commonly use thrust-related indications such as engine pressure ratio to monitor engine performance.

questions.question: Drives transmitter synchro rotor shaft:
questions.explanation: The mechanism sending information drives the transmitter synchro rotor shaft according to the measured position.

questions.question: Bevels, pinions gear in synchro represent:
questions.explanation: Gears such as bevel gears and pinions form part of the coupling element that transmits and modifies mechanical movement.

questions.question: Calibration of square law instruments based on:
questions.explanation: Airspeed-related instruments use the square-law relationship between dynamic pressure and airspeed for calibration.

questions.question: Purpose of sloping main instrument panel forward:
questions.explanation: Sloping the main instrument panel helps reduce parallax error by improving the pilot's viewing angle.

questions.question: Bourdon tube connected with hose acts as:
questions.explanation: The Bourdon tube detects pressure and its mechanical movement provides the measuring function.

questions.question: Carburetor intake air temperature indicator:
questions.explanation: Carburetor intake air temperature is an engine operating parameter, so its indicator is a powerplant instrument.

questions.question: Display governed by calibration logarithmic law:
questions.explanation: The rate of altitude change indication is identified as following a logarithmic calibration law in the provided material.

questions.question: International airworthiness laid down by:
questions.explanation: ICAO establishes international standards and recommended practices related to aviation and airworthiness.

questions.question: Where displacements are magnified and transmitted:
questions.explanation: The coupling element transmits mechanical displacement and can magnify the movement before it reaches the indicating element.

questions.question: Mechanism producing anti-backlash:
questions.explanation: The hairspring arrangement can provide an anti-backlash effect by maintaining tension in the mechanism.

questions.question: Airspeed range for flap extension indicated by:
questions.explanation: The white arc on an airspeed indicator represents the flap operating range.

questions.question: Two major components of a synchro:
questions.explanation: A basic synchro system consists primarily of a transmitter and receiver.

questions.question: Instrument mechanism system with elements in separate location:
questions.explanation: In a remote sensing instrument system, the sensing and indicating elements are located separately and information is transmitted between them.

questions.question: AC synchro system example:
questions.explanation: A differential synchro is an example of an AC synchro system.

questions.question: Instrument element sensing changes in physical quantity:
questions.explanation: The detecting element senses changes in the physical quantity being measured.

questions.question: Instruments included in basic six grouping:
questions.explanation: The altimeter and course indicator are included among the basic flight instrument grouping.

questions.question: Flange type instrument mounting has:
options: B. Front or rear end design
questions.explanation: Flange mounting instruments can have either a front-end or rear-end mounting design.

questions.question: Pressure type not requiring reference:
questions.explanation: Differential pressure measurement compares two pressures, rather than requiring a fixed absolute reference.

questions.question: Application of synchro system:
options: B. Remote position indication for autopilot
questions.explanation: Synchro systems can remotely transmit position information for systems such as autopilot controls.

questions.question: Panel visible straight to both pilot eyes:
questions.explanation: The main instrument panel is positioned so that its instruments are directly visible to both pilots.
